route_facts.interpretation: Wide losses are execution-cost scaling, not proposal-quality collapse or request-serial lowering.

named_blockers.C1: Production-D24 singleton keeps its direct/scalar proposal and replay economics; E1b begins at physical rows2 and E1a streaming is C3-only. The distinct strict natural25 automatic cell does not transfer to this comparator.
named_blockers.C2: One physical rows2 group and exact proposal-head reuse clear AR economics, but host prompt replay plus logical R8 target cost leave a 33.35% external gap. C3-only prompt streaming and R12 owners do not transfer.
named_blockers.C4: One physical rows4 group gets E1b proposal reuse, but keeps host prompt replay and logical R16 target decomposition; E2 owners are R12-only. Complete wall remains 24.54% below target.
named_blockers.C5: One outer rows5 group lowers proposals as rows4+1, so E1b already covers the non-singleton head. Host replay plus operation-complete logical R20 target/accept/commit/provider work leaves a 53.44% gap.
named_blockers.C6: One outer rows6 group lowers proposals as rows4+2; host replay plus logical R24 target/accept/commit/provider work leaves a 42.18% gap.
named_blockers.C7: One outer rows7 group lowers proposals as rows4+3; host replay plus logical R28 target/accept/commit/provider work leaves a 45.05% gap.
named_blockers.C8: One outer rows8 group lowers proposals as rows4+4; host replay plus logical R32 target/accept/commit/provider work leaves a 64.16% gap.
